answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with proof-of-useful-work staking: every identity keeps solving small verification tasks, climbing toward a summit of trust only real work reaches. Each solved task mints a jade token of reputation, non-transferable and tied to the identity that earned it. A meadow of honest agents grows as their jade accumulates, while an attacker spawning N fakes must pay N times the compute for every round. Forgery becomes a recurring compute tax: N fakes cost N workers' worth of electricity and time, pricing Sybils out by arithmetic.
